stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $ABCD$ with all four angles $90^\circ$ and side lengths $6$, $4$, $6$, $4$ in order around the shape.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call it a square as the label, with no check that all sides are equal.
Being a square is what produces the four right angles here.
It is a rectangle but not a square, because all angles are right while adjacent sides $6$ and $4$ are unequal.
Report $6$ as the type, because that numeral is printed first on a side.

teacher.key_rationale: All right angles make a rectangle; unequal adjacent sides mean it is not a square. Calling it a square by label swaps the class. Saying square-hood produces the right angles reverses the relation. Picking printed $6$ captures a surface number.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as rectangle ABCD with sides 6 and 4 and four right-angle marks.
